verdicts.strongest_argument: This is wire copy in the capture. The reverse split went out on PR Newswire on 2026-09-01 and is stored as a body (docs/ee32750e276846aba37596bed7e3b23135338ee9.txt) and indexed in snapshots/20260902T150801Z.json item 1, with the company's own 6-K in filings.json (accession 0001213900-26-096233, accepted 2026-09-01T20:30:01Z). A press release plus a same-evening 6-K is the maximum publication a nano-cap can achieve; there is nothing left for the market to learn. The interpretation - that a compliance reverse split says the company does not expect the price to recover on its own - is a truism about every reverse split ever announced, and a 1-for-10 is mechanically value-neutral. The corroboration offered is a second Stocktwits post in the very same stored document reading the sequence identically, which is publication, not independence. I also checked the tape, and the market repriced immediately: quote.json shows 0.388 on 08-31 falling to 0.373 on 09-01 and the baseline's completed 09-02 close at 0.343 (split-adjusted 3.43), i.e. -11.6% over the two sessions spanning the announcement. The claim that it cannot be priced because 'the stock would not have been bid 25% higher two sessions earlier on a pivot headline' compares the reaction to a different piece of news on a different day and does not survive contact with the intervening bars. Finally, the mechanism partly misses the print: the split takes effect at the 09-04 open, after the release, so its own price effect is a scheduled mechanical adjustment, not a print outcome.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Announces the 1-for-10 reverse share split effective at the 2026-09-04 Nasdaq open, expressly to regain minimum-bid-price compliance.
The company's own 6-K carrying the same announcement, on EDGAR the evening before the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json (unadjusted): 08-31 close 0.388, 09-01 close 0.373, and the baseline's completed 09-02 close of 0.343 on an adjusted basis of 3.43 - about -11.6% across the announcement, on declining volume from 182.7m to 6.9m shares. The market marked the stock down through the announcement. Baseline realised_vol_20d 114.6% and pct_from_52w_high -89.08% describe a name whose distress is already fully in the price.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence in the capture of a Nasdaq deficiency letter with a stated compliance deadline, or a stockholder-equity or market-value-of-listed-securities shortfall, which would make delisting risk a live print issue rather than a solved bid-price mechanic.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The acquisition is a 6-K plus a snapshot item and the finding concedes the headline is priced. What is left - the shape of the flow - is quote.json, the one file that is by construction public. I verified the arithmetic and it holds on an unadjusted basis: quote.json's 2026-08-31 bar is 182,733,300 shares at a 0.388 close, which against a 13.0-13.5m float is roughly thirteen turns, and the market cap of $5.48m at that price implies about 16m shares out, so the ratio is real rather than a units error. But that is precisely why it is priced: a nano-cap that turns thirteen times its float in one session, halts up, runs 35% and closes only 8.4% higher has been repriced in public, in the most visible way a stock can be, and the round-trip over the following two sessions (0.388 to 0.373 to 0.343) is the market completing that judgement before the print. The finding's own conclusion - distribution into retail - is the market's verdict on the pivot, not information withheld from it. One caution on the numbers the hunter and I are both using: quote.json here is unadjusted for the 1-for-10 split while the baseline is adjusted, and the 09-02 bar in quote.json (0.3097, 1,299,693 shares, fetched 2026-09-02T15:08:01Z) is a partial intraday bar - a reader who mixed the two series would be out by a factor of ten. The dilution machinery in the independence field (F-1, F-3, 424B3/B5, two Form Ds) is all in filings.json and all months old; age is not novelty.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Announces the LightSolver acquisition and the entry into photonic computing, with consideration in newly issued shares and warrants.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: quote.json 08-31: 182,733,300 shares, close 0.388 after a halt and a ~35% intraday run; 09-01 0.373 on 6,877,000; completed 09-02 close 0.343 per baseline. Baseline history records the 08-31 event at +8.38% with event_day_volume 18,273,330 on its adjusted basis. run_up_5d +11.36% and run_up_20d +10.65% into the print. The full round-trip inside two sessions is the clearest possible statement that the tape has already judged the pivot.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Disclosure of the share and warrant count issued for LightSolver, sized against the ~16m shares outstanding, which would convert 'paper consideration' from a characterisation into a measurable dilution figure.

verdicts.strongest_argument: The three 13D/A accessions are in filings.json with dates, so they were reachable, but nothing in the capture draws out who filed them, for how many shares, or in which direction - the bodies are not stored and the hunter says so. That is the reachable-but-unconnected band and I will not score it higher. What caps it is size and mechanism rather than publication. This is a $5.5m market cap; a >5% holder's position moving 'materially' is a few hundred thousand dollars, and against a session in which 182.7m shares changed hands the supply implication of three amendments is not measurable. A 13D/A also reports a position change that has already occurred, so it describes flow behind the tape, not in front of it, and the last of the three is dated 2026-08-21, before the 08-31 volume event that would have absorbed any of it. The finding correctly says this collapses into the same EDGAR-index cluster as #1, so it is not a second observation.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Three 13D amendments were publicly indexed on EDGAR between 07-27 and 08-21, ahead of the print.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: No distinguishable price or volume signature on 07-27, 07-31 or 08-21 in the bars; the series is quiet in the 6-20k share range until the 08-31 event. That is consistent with reachable-but-unnoticed, which is why this is 30 rather than 15, and equally consistent with immaterial.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A 13D/A body naming a holder whose remaining registrable stake is large relative to the ~16m shares outstanding and still unsold under the live resale shelf.

interactions: #1 and #2 rest on the same filings.json index and the hunter concedes #2 should collapse into #1. #0 and #1 both rest on the sequence of pre-print disclosures and both use the same tape; taken together they are one story - a distressed nano-cap doing a pivot and a compliance split in the same week - published in full across two press releases and two 6-Ks. A units trap runs through all three: quote.json is unadjusted for the 1-for-10 split while the baseline is adjusted, and the 08-31 volume differs by exactly 10x between them.
corpus_limits: No 13D/A body, and no share or warrant count for the LightSolver consideration, is stored, so neither dilution nor holder identity is verifiable here. CLGN's baseline carries event_plausibility 'unknown' with cadence_implausible and a last_print of 2026-09-01 only two days earlier, and the capture directory is dated 2026-09-02 against a 2026-09-03 event date, so I cannot confirm from this capture that a results release occurred on 2026-09-03 rather than having already been made on 09-01; I scored the findings on their own terms but that uncertainty should temper all three.
